simple.meaning: נָשַׁל (nâshal) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to pluck off , i.e. divest , eject or drop.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 7 times across Exodus, Deuteronomy, Joshua, 2 Kings, beginning at Exodus 3:5. Its contexts include land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָשַׁל (H5394).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: נָשַׁל (nâshal) / H5394 is traced through Exodus 3:5, Deuteronomy 7:1, Deuteronomy 7:22, Deuteronomy 19:5 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: He said, “Don’t come close. Take off your sandals, for the place you are standing on is holy ground.”

When Yahweh your God brings you into the land where you go to possess it, and casts out many nations before you—the Hittite, the Girgashite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite—seven nations greater and mightier than you;
Yahweh your God will cast out those nations before you little by little. You may not consume them at once, lest the animals of the field increase on you.

as when a man goes into the forest with his neighbor to chop wood and his hand swings the ax to cut down the tree, and the head slips from the handle and hits his neighbor so that he dies—he shall flee to one of these cities and live.
You will have olive trees throughout all your borders, but you won’t anoint yourself with the oil, for your olives will drop off.
The prince of Yahweh’s army said to Joshua, “Take off your sandals, for the place on which you stand is holy.” Joshua did so.
At that time Rezin king of Syria recovered Elath to Syria, and drove the Jews from Elath; and the Syrians came to Elath, and lived there, to this day.

definitions.short: to pluck off , i.e. divest , eject or drop
definitions.usage: cast (out), drive, loose, put off (out), slip.
definitions.full: H5394. nashal נָשַׁל verb 1. intransitive slip or drop off ; also transitive: 2 draw off . 3 clear away (Late Hebrew נָשַׁל probably intransitive, Qal not used, but noun נְשִׁילָה a falling off , etc.; Pi`el, Hiph`il cast off, let fall off , Niph`al be cast off, fall off ; ᵑ7 Aph`el אַשֵּׁיל cast out (from house); Arabic excidit pluma, etc.; but also transitive, avis mutavit rejecitque plumas (Frey); — celeriter extraxit , etc., is denominative from loan-word according to Frä 88 ); — Qal Perfect וְנָשַׁל consecutive Deut 7:1-2 t.; Imperfect 3masculine singular יִשַּׁל 28:40 ; Imperative masculine singular שַׁל Exod 3:5 ; Josh 5:15 ; — 1 slip or drop off , מִןהָֿעֵץ הַבַּרְזֶל וְנָשַׁל Deut 19:5 and the iron slippeth off from the wood (i.e. axe-head from helve); זֵיתֶ֑ךָ יִשַּׁל 28:40 thine olives shall drop off (absolute). 2 draw off sandal from ( מֵעַל ) foot Exod 3:5 (E), Josh 5:15 (JE). 3 clear away nations מִמָּנֶיךָ Deut 7:1 , 22 . Pi`el Imperfect 3masculine singular וַיְנַשֵּׁל 2Kin 16:6 he cleared the Jews entirely out of ( מִן ) Elath.
